source.title: LLM Circuit Analyses Are Consistent Across Training and Scale
source.authors: Curt Tigges; Michael Hanna; Qi-Nan Yu; Stella Biderman

page_placements.theme: Training changes IOI mechanisms and their causal signs

record.tranche_reason: The study tests IOI circuit structure and roles in Pythia models using path patching and logit difference, the original study's causal method and task measure, but in different models and training checkpoints.
record.gate_note: The paper analyzes Pythia IOI circuits across checkpoints and scales, and reports path-patching results for the three circuit stages. Its 80% whole-model-performance threshold is used to select circuits, not reported as an independent outcome. The IOI behavioral curves in Figure 1 establish task acquisition but do not by themselves measure circuit identity or roles. The paper does not test GPT-2 small, the original 26-head/seven-class circuit, backup-head takeover after ablation, or robustness to alternative methods, ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions.
record.test_reason: The study applies the original's path patching and IOI logit-difference measure to Pythia-160m through 2.8b across training checkpoints. It asks whether the same head classes and their algorithmic roles carry IOI, which bears directly on V3 for other sizes and checkpoints.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the IOI algorithm and its component types are stable across training and similar across Pythia scales, despite head turnover and small class differences (no duplicate-token heads in 160m). They caution that this covers simple tasks and one model family.
record.recipe_differences: Uses path patching and IOI logit difference to assess algorithmic roles, as in the original analysis, but uses EAP-IG to find circuits and studies Pythia checkpoints rather than GPT-2 small. The circuit selection uses an 80% performance threshold; completeness is acknowledged as difficult to establish.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual heads lose their function late in training and other heads take over the role while IOI performance stays stable. For example, Pythia-160m head (4,6) is a name mover from 4×10^9 to 3×10^10 tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Head identity in the IOI circuit turns over during training while the class-level algorithm persists (load-balancing over training).

fits_no_version.finding: IOI circuit node count correlates with model size (r=0.72). Node-set Jaccard similarity fluctuates and is more stable in larger models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuit size scales with model size, with roles diffused across more heads.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2024 is stated in the paper text; supplied venue metadata says Workshop on Representation Learning for NLP.
record.problems: Circuit tests cover only Pythia-160m through Pythia-2.8b; Pythia-70m does not learn IOI, and Pythia-6.9b/12b are omitted from circuit finding. Exact path-patching values are plotted rather than stated numerically. The authors note that circuit completeness is difficult to verify and that their tasks and model family are limited.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1's checkpoint-by-checkpoint IOI behavioral curves are not included as circuit-role rows; they report task performance rather than circuit identity or causal roles. Component-score trajectories in Figures 2–3 beyond the name-mover emergence range and the specific head change in R16 are not separately extracted because they do not independently test the same-class-and-role IOI circuit claim.

untested.parts: GPT-2 small, the 26-head / 7-class circuit and the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests are not examined.
No ablation-induced takeover of name-mover heads is quantified. Only a Figure 4A legend note on negative heads exists (see missing).
Other model families and architectures; Pythia-6.9b and 12b circuits; Pythia-70m (does not learn IOI); reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
EAP-IG circuits are not compared against other methods, ablations or metrics.
No variation of ablation type, metric or prompt distribution. The 80% threshold is a selection setting.
Only a 70-example IOI set from the Wang generator is used; no name-order, template or more-names variants.

missing.what: Copy-suppression heads contribute positively to the Pythia IOI circuit (downweighting the incorrect name), reversing their negative role in GPT-2 small.

Pythia-160m circuit diagram lists negative name-mover / copy-suppression heads 9.1 and 9.5 that reduce their negativity when name movers are ablated. The paper frames this as self-repair; it is stated qualitatively only.
Circuit size versus model size correlation for IOI (r=0.72) and Jaccard stability of node sets.

record.verdict_notes: Per-model path-patching values are figure-only; the text states only aggregate thresholds. Circuits were found with EAP-IG at an 80% performance threshold, with path patching used for role verification. The paper header says NeurIPS 2024. The V2 negative-head self-repair note is a figure-legend statement without numbers, so no V2 verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: The specific GPT-2 small circuit, its 26 attention heads and seven classes, and the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.

Whether ablating main name-mover heads causes backup heads to take over. The authors observe changing head functions over training and suggest self-repair as a possibility, but do not test takeover caused by ablation.

Other model families and architectures; circuit analyses above Pythia-2.8B (Pythia-6.9B and 12B are omitted from circuit finding); reuse of IOI circuit components for other tasks. The study tests Pythia training checkpoints and scales, not the broad claim about component reuse.
Whether alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same circuit.
Whether faithfulness or completeness changes with ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution, and whether the circuit explains only part of behavior under those alternatives.
Circuit behavior across name orders, templates, and prompts with more names.

rows.measure: Stability of relative path-patching contributions to IOI circuit stages
rows.value: The authors state scores remain stable after circuit formation, with no dramatic shifts corresponding to functional-component changes; scores are generally above 50%, and copy-suppression/name-mover scores are above 70%.
rows.note: The paper reports this conclusion across the analyzed models; exact values are presented only in plots.
rows.check: Aggregate summary of R1–R12, drawn from the same Figure 4B–D statement. Not independent evidence; avoid double counting.

rows.subject: Pythia-160m, Pythia-410m, Pythia-1.4b, and Pythia-2.8b
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative comparison of end-of-training IOI circuit head classes
rows.measure: Presence of head classes and their algorithmic roles
rows.value: Name-mover, copy-suppression, and S-inhibition heads occur in all analyzed circuits; Pythia-160m lacks duplicate-token heads that occur in the others.
rows.note: The authors characterize the circuits as broadly similar but note this class-level difference.
rows.check: Should also note that copy-suppression heads change sign of role: positive in Pythia IOI (downweight the wrong name) versus negative in GPT-2 (Section 3.2, Appendix D).

rows.subject: Pythia-160m
rows.operation_detail: Tracking individual head functional scores over training
rows.measure: Name-mover functional behavior of the identified head
rows.value: The head acquires name-mover behavior after 4 × 10^9 tokens and stops exhibiting it at 3 × 10^10 tokens.
rows.note: This is a change in a particular head's behavior over training; the paper reports that other heads can take its place, while the overall IOI behavior remains stable.

relationships.condition: Pythia-160m, 410m, 1.4b and 2.8b, checkpoints after circuit formation
relationships.reason: Path-patching shares are stable: CS/NM above 70%, S-inhibition and tertiary stages generally above 50%, with no algorithm shifts (R1–R13). Name-mover heads emerge at 2–8×10^9 tokens across sizes (R15).
relationships.display_finding: Path-patching shares remain above 70% for copy suppression and name movers and generally above 50% for S-inhibition and tertiary stages, without algorithm shifts; name movers emerge at 2–8 billion training tokens.

relation.reason: The study directly tests recurrence and stability of IOI component classes and roles across Pythia sizes and training checkpoints.

tranche.reason: Algorithmic verification uses the original IOI path-patching method and logit-difference measure, although circuit discovery uses EAP-IG.

source_check.notes: R13 summarizes R1–R12 rather than providing independent evidence. Appendix A.1 defines absolute-effect ratios; these are not completeness scores, and the reported thresholds are aggregate textual summaries rather than exact per-checkpoint values.

statements.correction: No causal role-preserving cross-task reuse test is reported. Section 3.2 describes induction heads as supporting IOI and Greater-Than; Figure 2 tracks induction-head component scores for Greater-Than.
statements.problem: Causal role-preserving cross-task reuse is untested, but this paper does not explicitly identify that omission as future work.
